The two terms in this equation are explained as follows: n When firms expect a high price level, they expect high costs. Those firms that fix prices in advance set their prices high. These high prices cause the other firms to set high prices also. Hence, a high expected price level EP leads to a high actual price level P. This effect does not depend on the fraction of firms with sticky prices. n When output is high, the demand for goods is high. Those firms with flexible prices set their prices high, which leads to a high price level. The effect of output on the price level depends on the fraction of firms with sticky prices. The more firms that have sticky prices, the less the price level responds to the level of economic activity.
